To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the three new triterpene glycosides were isolated from Glycyrrhizae radix (licorice), and their structure was determined by spectroscopic methods.
three new oleanane saponins (1–3), one artificial compound (4), five known triterpenoid glucuronides (6–10) were isolated from the root of Glycyrrrhiza glabra.
three new oleanane triterpene glycosides (1–3), one artificial product (4) and five known triterpenes (5–9) were isolated from the root of Glycyrriza glabra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of new triterpene glycosides, and the preliminary evaluation of their neuraminidase inhibitory activity, which is a potential target for anti-influenza virus drug design.
the isolation, identification, and bioactivity of oleanane triterpene glycosides from the roots of G. glabra.
the chemical investigation of the triterpene glycosides from the roots of G. glabra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a glucuronide moiety is essential for the neuraminidase inhibitory effect of oleanane triterpene derivatives.

the presence of a sugar chain at C-3 of the aglycone is crucial for the inhibition of neuraminidase, and that the presence of an acetyl group at O-3 of the sugar chain is important for enhancing inhibitory activity.

compounds 2 and 4 exhibited the most potent inhibitory activities against neuraminidase with IC50 values of 0.23 and 0.24 μM, respectively, which are more potent than that of the positive control (oseltamivir phosphate, IC50 = 0.26 μM).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the triterpene aglycones and their glucuronide conjugates were found to be active against influenza virus neuraminidase, and that the aglycones are more potent than the glucuronides.

the structure of the triterpene aglycon and the number of glucuronide moieties are the main factors influencing the inhibitory effects of triterpene trisaccharides against neuraminidase, and that the presence of a glucuronic acid moiety at the C-3 position is crucial for inhibitory activity.
compound 2, which was a novel compound, exhibited the strongest inhibitory effect, with an IC 50 value of 1.3 μM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oleanane-type glycoside 4 showed a strong neuraminidase inhibitory activity, with an IC 50 value of 1.2 μM, which was better than the positive control (oseltamivir, IC 50 value 3.0 μM).

the presence of a sugar moiety at C-3 and the number and position of the hydroxyl groups on the aglycone are the main structural factors that influence the neuraminidase-inhibitory activity of oleanane triterpene glycosides.
licorice-sapogenin O4 is the most promising neuraminidase inhibitor among all of the tested triterpenes, and it has an IC50 value of 2.4 ± 0.2 µM.
